verdict.rationale: The README covers the main pieces of a rig bring-up. It names the hardware (a $7 ESP32 plus a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter for Lightning phones) and describes the connection (USB-C plugs in directly, and the phone powers the board). It also gives a flashing entry point: always build with flash.sh, which applies the BLE buffer config. Beyond that, it has a four-step self-checking setup and a board test tool for debugging. However, the evidence shows only fragments rather than a complete end-to-end procedure. Missing for 10: an explicit bill of materials with the exact ESP32 board model, step-by-step flashing instructions (toolchain, prerequisites, commands), and independent or hands-on confirmation that the bring-up can be followed end to end.
